title.value: Dissecting Deep RL with High Update Ratios: Combatting Value Divergence
title.justification: The title succinctly captures the primary focus of the research, which is exploring the challenges and solutions associated with high update ratios in deep reinforcement learning and the problem of value divergence, as evident throughout the paper.
title.quote: We employ a simple unit-ball normalization that enables learning under large update ratios, show its efficacy on the widely used dm_control suite, and obtain strong performance on the challenging dog tasks, competitive with model-based approaches.

analysis.description: This paper investigates the challenges of training deep reinforcement learning (RL) models under high update-to-data ratios, specifically addressing the issue of value function divergence. It proposes using unit-ball normalization to manage this divergence, demonstrating its effectiveness through empirical experiments on the dm_control suite and challenging dog tasks, aiming to make high-update training more efficient and reliable.

type.justification: The study extensively discusses empirical experiments and results, showcasing evidence from practical implementations of techniques like unit-ball normalization on the dm_control MuJoCo benchmarks, and comparing the performance of models.
type.quote: We employ a simple unit-ball normalization that enables learning under large update ratios, show its efficacy on the widely used dm_control suite, and obtain strong performance on the challenging dog tasks, competitive with model-based approaches.
